In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the properties of ion channels in dystrophic muscles and the identification of the molecular components of the channels.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the absence of dystphin has no effect on sarcolemmal Na+, K+, Ca2+ and Cl- channel function, but it does affect the distribution of Na+, Ca2+ channels and Na+/K+-ATPase.
dystrophin deficiency has a profound impact on ion channel function in dystrophic skeletal muscle.
, although there are some differences in the properties of ion channels in dystrophic fibres, these are not sufficient to cause a major change in membrane potential and Ca2+ homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in DMD, the distribution and function are normal for most ion channels.
in dystrophin deficient fibres, the properties of sarcolema ion channels are not altered, except for the voltage-gated K+ channel Kv1.1, which is down-regulated.
, in DMD muscle, the sarcolemmal Na+ and K+ channels are normal in terms of their density, kinetics and regulation by Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of dystropin has no effect on the distribution or function of the sarcolemmal K+ channels.
, in dystrophin deficient skeletal muscle fibres, the expression and function of voltage-dependent Na+ channels and voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels is altered.
dystrophin deficiency has little or no impact on the expression and function of sarcolemal ion channels, at least at the level of the whole fibre.
